summary: The draft is broadly well cited, but the nearest comparator literature (benchmark-level score prediction, matrix completion and adaptive testing on LLM score matrices), the Open LLM Leaderboard data source, and the intro's benchmark-redundancy premise each need 1-3 targeted citations.
missing_literatures: cross-benchmark score prediction and matrix completion on LLM evaluation matrices
adaptive or IRT-based test and benchmark selection for LLM evaluation
Open LLM Leaderboard and its component benchmarks
empirical evidence of benchmark redundancy and correlation

rewrite_targets.reason: The closest prior work is benchmark-level: predicting unrun benchmark scores from a few observed ones, low-rank or matrix-completion imputation of LLM score matrices, and adaptive or active selection of what to run. The Related Work text names matrix completion as 'the standard alternatives for filling score matrices' but cites only generic sources (Candes, Salakhutdinov). The novelty claim ('here the unit of selection is a whole benchmark and the target is every benchmark not run') is therefore not positioned against the work that most directly competes with it.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: Low-rank and probabilistic matrix completion ... are the standard alternatives for filling score matrices; These works reduce item counts; here the unit of selection is a whole benchmark
search_topics: predicting LLM performance on unseen benchmarks from a subset of benchmark scores
matrix completion or low-rank factorization of model-by-benchmark score matrices
adaptive testing or IRT-based active selection for LLM evaluation

rewrite_targets.reason: The motivating premise, that benchmark suites 'are known to overlap in what they measure', is supported only by citations to the suites themselves. Those papers do not document redundancy or correlation among benchmarks, so the premise that makes budgeted evaluation worthwhile is thinly supported.
rewrite_targets.anchor_text: are known to overlap in what they measure
search_topics: correlation or redundancy among LLM benchmarks
low-dimensional structure in LLM benchmark scores

rewrite_targets.reason: The Open LLM Leaderboard is one of the three sealed evaluation datasets, and its six component benchmarks (IFEval, BBH, MATH Level 5, GPQA, MuSR, MMLU-Pro) appear by name in the protocol and appendix. None of them has a citation, although HELM and MTEB are cited. A reviewer would expect a source for the leaderboard and its benchmarks.
